title: Economic development
examples: What are some key indicators we can use to measure development?
Can you explain the difference between aid and trade in development?
What are the biggest barriers preventing developing nations from growing?

explain.say: Today we will explore what economic development means for countries.
One key indicator is the Gross Domestic Product per capita.

items: Row 1: GDP per capita | Currency unit

draw.text: GDP per capita: Total GDP / Population

explain.say: Another important measure is the Human Development Index.
Barriers can include political instability or conflict.
Trade imbalances are also major economic barriers for nations.
Strategies involve improving infrastructure and education access.

faq.q: How is GDP per capita different from just total GDP?
faq.a: GDP per capita takes the total output and divides it by the population. This gives you a per person measure of wealth.
asks: What does per capita mean in economics?
Is total GDP enough to judge a country?

faq.q: Are there any indicators that only look at wealth?
faq.a: No, the Human Development Index looks beyond just money. It includes health and education levels too.
asks: What is the best measure of development?
Does money tell the whole story about a country?

faq.q: Does political instability always stop development?
faq.a: It makes development very difficult because businesses fear losing their investments. Stable governance is very important.
asks: Can a country develop with bad politics?

faq.q: Is trade deficit always bad for a country?
faq.a: Not necessarily, but a persistent one means the country relies heavily on imports. It needs to manage its external debt carefully.
asks: What is the difference between trade deficit and trade surplus?
When is it okay to borrow money from other countries?

faq.q: Is foreign aid always the best strategy?
faq.a: No, aid can sometimes create dependency. Combining aid with trade agreements is often a more balanced strategy.
asks: Should a country rely on foreign aid?
What is the role of international organizations?

facts: GDP per capita measures average economic output per person.
The Human Development Index combines income, health, and education.
Political stability is crucial for attracting long-term investment.
Diversifying exports helps reduce reliance on single markets.

quiz.say: A country has a high total GDP but very low life expectancy. Which indicator suggests a problem?
quiz.why: The HDI combines multiple factors, so low life expectancy signals a problem beyond just income.

wrong.0: This only measures income and ignores health outcomes.
wrong.1: This is a total figure and does not tell you about the average person.
wrong.2: This relates to trade balance, not human well-being.

quiz.say: If a country constantly buys more goods than it sells, what is its likely issue?
quiz.why: Buying more than selling creates a deficit, which is a major economic barrier.

wrong.0: This is a strategy, not the description of the economic problem itself.
wrong.2: High GDP suggests strong overall production, not necessarily trade balance.
wrong.3: Literacy is a positive indicator, but it does not fix a trade imbalance.

quiz.say: Which combination of strategies is most effective for sustained growth?
quiz.why: Combining market access with human capital development creates a cycle of growth.

wrong.1: This can lead to dependency without building local capacity.
wrong.2: Roads are useless if people are not educated enough to use them.
wrong.3: This is unsustainable and ignores the need for diversified industries.
